predecessors.note: The Abe were 'the general overseeing the Emishi' in 1050; the land is the Emishi domains left after 802 (emishi dossier), vassal tint of heian-japan from about 850.

land.text: the Abe lands after the 'Imperial victory' at Kuriyagawa in 1062, held by the court's governors with the Kiyohara of Dewa

successors.note: The Former Nine Years' War page does not say who held the Abe land afterwards; it names a Governor 'from the Kiyohara clan' who supplied troops. The heian-japan dossier draws the land as Heian's own from 1062 to 1086.

capitals.name: Koromo Stockade (Hiraizumi area)
capitals.note: Abe no Yoritoki page: his son Norito 'stayed at the Koromo Stockade with his father'; Yoritoki died 28 August 1057. The page gives no coordinates: the Koromo River at Hiraizumi is the researcher's placement.

capitals.name: Kuriyagawa Stockade (Morioka area)
capitals.note: Sadato 'occupied the Kuriyagawa Stockade' (Yoritoki page); the 1062 assault on the Kuriyagawa fortress ended the war (Former Nine Years' War page). Coordinates are the researcher's placement at Morioka; the page gives none.

correction.text: the six Emishi districts of the Kitakami Basin 'from Morioka to Hiraizumi' and the Emishi domains around them, 'Mutsu province, Tohoku region'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a rebel state Cliopatria lacks (its Northern Fujiwara row starts only in 1094). The same land as the emishi dossier's 802-1051 shape: the Heian dossier uses Cliopatria's Northern Fujiwara 1094 outline for the 'Abe lands' and the two differ by 7 of about 130 cells. The Yoritoki page says the Abe were 'allowed to rule the six Emishi districts' of the Kitakami Basin, from Morioka to Hiraizumi, a smaller core than the drawn shape; no page gives an area.

region.text: the six Emishi districts of the Kitakami Basin 'from Morioka to Hiraizumi' and the Emishi domains around them, 'Mutsu province, Tohoku region'

ledger.note: 1051: Abe no Yoritoki defies the court. 'In 1050, the general overseeing the Emishi was Abe no Yoritoki', who 'levied taxes and confiscated property on his own'; the war is dated 1051-1062 and, on the Yoritoki page, begins when he defeats a government army at Onikiribe in 1051. The page gives the lands as Mutsu, not a boundary.

region.text: 'Mutsu province, Tohoku region', the Abe lands

ledger.note: 1051: Yoritoki 'led Emishi forces into northern Miyagi and defeated a government army at Onikiribe', which 'triggered the Former Nine Years' War'; Minamoto no Yoriyoshi was sent against him in 1053 as Chinjufu Shogun. Zone mirrors the heian-japan dossier's contest.

1062: Kuriyagawa falls. 'In 1062, Minamoto no Yoriyoshi, along with his son, led an assault on an Abe fortress at Kuriyagawa'; 'After two days of fighting, Sadato surrendered'; infobox 'Imperial victory'. Major battles were rare until Kawasaki (1057), where Sadato beat the Minamoto; Yoritoki had died on 28 August 1057 (Yoritoki page).

1062: the Abe are crushed. His sons 'finally overwhelmed' by combined Minamoto and Kiyowara armies (Yoritoki page); the land goes to the court's governors (the Kiyohara of Dewa supplied troops; the page gives no division of the land).

wars.name: Former Nine Years' War
wars.outcome: Imperial victory: Abe no Sadato surrendered at Kuriyagawa in 1062; the Abe lands passed to the court's governors.
wars.note: Infobox 1051-1062. The Yoritoki page puts the outbreak of full war in 1057 ('War erupted in 1057'); the Minamoto commander arrived in 1053 there.

certainty.note: Only fortresses (Koromo, Kuriyagawa, Isawa, Kurosawa) are named; no boundary is given.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from two pages (Former Nine Years' War, Abe no Yoritoki). Type rebel: the Abe held Mutsu against the court for eleven years. The Abe clan of Emishi 'emerged from the Appi River basin' early in the 9th century and supplied generals and governors (Yoritoki page), so the clan existed long before 1051; the dossier covers only the revolt, matching the heian-japan ledger (contest_start 'Abe clan' 1051, gain 1062). Counterpart string 'Abe clan' in heian-japan = this slug. No rulers list (Yoritoki d. 1057; Sadato led to 1062 but the page gives no reign). Capitals' coordinates are the researcher's placement of stockades named on the pages. The Kiyohara (1062-1087, Gosannen War 1083-1089 'disputed', infobox 'Military stalemate') held Dewa and Mutsu next; the Gosannen War page says nothing on the Kiyohara's land, so no kiyohara-clan dossier was written (a gap-filler could open the Kiyohara clan and Northern Fujiwara pages). Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
